supersedes: R121F (2/10) which measured a one-verb policy and R121G-style 3/10 which was contaminated by a start-up race

design.policy: one generic policy, six verbs: click-text, select-from-list, multi-select by comma/and, click-link-text, type-into-field, colour-match-by-computed-background, nested-menu A>B>C, plus submit
design.race_fixed: the earlier NO-VERB failures were caused by reading #query before the episode populated it; the policy now polls up to 3s for a non-empty goal after starting

results.failure: link text 'nunc' not exposed as a clickable element with accessible text
target is a glyph 'x', not text
level 1 opened but submenu 'Ariana' never became hit-testable
goal names a colour; no text target exists at all
dropdown options are not in the DOM until the select is opened

finding: all five failures have the same class. None is a missing verb: type, multi-select, click and submit all work. Every failure is a failure to LOCATE a target that is not a text-labelled element in the DOM.
why_click_color_is_decisive: the goal is 'Click on the olive colored box'. There is no text to match, ever. No amount of stored procedure or instant learning can address an unlabelled visual target. This is the clean counterexample to 'learn it once and computer use is solved'.
relationship_to_literature: MMBench-GUI (CVPR 2026): 'Accurate visual grounding is the primary driver of success'; 'Action-space bottlenecks: many failures stem from missing or overly coarse primitives, not perception alone' -- the two are separated, and this measurement lands on the grounding side
ComponentBench (COLM 2026): five critical interactions at 80% reliability imply a ~33% end-to-end ceiling -- memory does not raise a reliability ceiling it does not touch
ScratchWorld (2026): planning-mode 78.3% vs primitive-mode 14.5%; perception 90.5% vs single-step drag 23.3% -- reasoning is not the bottleneck for execution
the_first_principles_statement: learning is a multiplier on capability, not an addition to it. If grounding is g on a task, perfect memory gives g x 1.0 = g. The only way to move the product is to raise g.
what_is_NOT_claimed: that 5/10 is the project's reach on MiniWob++ (130 tasks; this is a biased 10-task sample chosen because they are the ones the earlier policy failed)
that the other 120 tasks distribute like these
that the verb set is complete
